problems.title: Bayesian linear-regression information loss omits observation noise
problems.source_location: Appendix D.6, Example 4, p.28; common proof p.29.
claim: Example \(4\) substitutes X Sigma X-transpose into a future-observation Gaussian determinant ratio.
analysis: Use prior variance \(2\), observation-noise variance \(2\), and repeated scalar input \(1\). After one observation, latent posterior variance is \(1\). Two future latent values therefore have singular covariance \(\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\), so the printed noise-free determinant ratio diverges. Future observations instead have covariance \(K=\begin{pmatrix}3&1\\1&3\end{pmatrix}\), giving finite divergence \(\frac12\log(9/8)\simeq0.0588915178\). The covariance does not depend on the observed response.
result: Example4 omits observation-noise covariance and can return a divergent expression for a finite Gaussian information loss.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Use future-observation covariance \(K=X\Sigma X^\top+\tau^2I\) and the Gaussian ratio \(\det(\operatorname{diag}K)/\det K\), with the stated input/context expectations.
problems.impact_rationale: The future-observation information-loss calculation omits observation noise and can diverge where the correct Gaussian quantity is finite. This is a substantial failure of the paper's mathematical example.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: The GP formula mixes KL directions
claim: Example \(5\) names forward \(\operatorname{KL}(P\|Q)\), but uses the precision of \(P\) in trace and mean terms.
analysis: For equal means, \(K_P=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\Sigma_Q=2I\), the printed mixed expression gives \(0.4771743696\). Forward KL is \(\frac12\log(4/3)\simeq0.1438410362\), while reverse KL is \(0.1894922971\). Thus swapping the labels does not fix the formula. Positive observation noise makes both Gaussian laws nonsingular.
result: Example5 mixes forward and reverse Gaussian-KL terms; neither direction agrees with the printed expression.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: For forward \(\operatorname{KL}(P\|Q)\), retain the corresponding determinant ratio and use \(\Sigma_Q^{-1}\) in trace and mean-quadratic terms. The conditional-information chain identities are not refuted.
problems.impact_rationale: The GP divergence formula combines opposite KL directions and equals neither on nonsingular Gaussian inputs, a substantial derivation error in the core information-loss calculation.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: The public acquisition order is fixed rather than sequential
claim: Algorithm 3 recomputes uncertainty after each queried label.
analysis: The script scores every candidate once before the budget loop, then repeatedly takes the first \(k\) entries of that fixed ordering. Consider two duplicate GP candidates of prior variance \(1\) and an independent candidate of variance \(0.6\), with noise \(0.01\). Querying one duplicate reduces the other's variance to \(0.01/1.01\simeq0.00990099\); sequential uncertainty selection then chooses the independent point, whereas fixed ranking need not.
result: The released active-learning path uses a fixed initial uncertainty ranking rather than the sequential rule in Algorithm3.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Move score computation, one query and context update into one loop, or label the existing method as fixed-ranking batch acquisition. Historical figure attribution remains unknown.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: The rollout statistic is a final predictive mean
claim: Algorithm 3 averages all J generated samples within each path before comparing paths.
analysis: The release records the final predictive mean, rather than averaging all \(J\) generated samples along the path. For latent variance \(v\) and noise variance \(\tau^2\), the path-mean variance is \(v+\tau^2/J\), while the final-predictive-mean variance is \(v-v\tau^2/[\tau^2+(J-1)v]\). At \(v=\tau^2=1,J=1\), they are \(2\) and zero; at \(J=20\), they are \(1.05\) and \(0.95\). Both approach \(v\), so the alternative statistic is not automatically useless.
result: The release uses a final predictive mean instead of the declared within-path sample mean. Its asymptotic agreement does not make the finite statistics equal.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Compute the stated path-sample mean or explicitly define and analyze the alternate finite-path estimator. Corrected learning curves are not asserted.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
